benchmarks.name: Event prose
benchmarks.original:
The catering quote from Saffron Bites just came in. For the main spread on the 15th, they're offering two tiers. Tier A is $48 per head and includes the seared tuna canapés, the braised short rib station, and the full dessert display. Tier B, at $37 per head, swaps the short rib for a mushroom Wellington station and cuts the dessert display down to just the chocolate torte and berry pavlovas. My read is we need to stick with Tier A for the primary sponsor dinner in the Veridian Room, but we could potentially use Tier B for the general attendee reception in the Atrium if the budget gets squeezed. However, their minimum for any single service is 70 guests.

If our final headcount for the Veridian Room is under 70, we’ll need to pad it with organizing committee members to hit the minimum, but please only move people from the Atrium list if absolutely necessary; we promised them the full experience. For the Atrium, if the count is between 70 and 90, Tier B is approved. If it exceeds 90, switch back to Tier A for them as well, as the per-head cost difference shrinks with volume and the upgrade is worth it for the larger crowd.

On timing: they need the final menu selection and guaranteed guest numbers by 5 p.m. this Thursday, the 7th. They’ve offered a 3% discount if we wire the 50% deposit by Friday at noon instead of the following Monday. The remaining balance is due on the 13th. Please confirm the wire details with Aris in Finance and use vendor code CAT-882. If the discount applies, note it explicitly on the payment authorization. Also, double-check that their proposal includes the late-night snack delivery for the tech crew at 11 p.m.—that’s a separate order for 15 boxed meals and shouldn’t be part of the per-head calculation.

Crucially, if we go with Tier B anywhere, you must get written confirmation from Saffron Bites that all nut-based ingredients are excluded from the mushroom Wellington filling. Last year’s incident with the pine nut puree cannot be repeated. Their standard recipe includes it, so this requires a specific amendment.

Event date is the 15th.
Tier A costs $48 per person.
Tier A includes seared tuna canapés, braised short rib station, and full dessert display.
Tier B costs $37 per person.
Tier B includes mushroom Wellington station (instead of short rib) and limited desserts (chocolate torte and berry pavlovas).
Tier A is for the primary sponsor dinner in the Veridian Room.

Remaining balance is due on the 13th.

benchmarks.name: Equipment procedure
benchmarks.original:
The secondary hydrostatic test on Vessel C-18A is not proceeding within nominal parameters. At approximately 10:47 local, after achieving the target 22.5 MPa hold pressure, we observed a persistent pressure decay of 0.08 MPa per minute over a five-minute monitoring period, exceeding the acceptable threshold of 0.02 MPa per minute defined in procedure MNT-VSL-7. The test medium is potable water at 15°C. I have suspended the test at 10:52 and initiated a controlled depressurization at a rate not exceeding 0.3 MPa per minute. The drain valve, DV-7, is currently open to the containment sump.

Before any re-test can be authorized, a full inspection of the primary weld seam, Weld-Series Gamma, is required. This is the longitudinal seam fabricated by Contractor Arclight. The inspection must use the portable phased-array ultrasonic tester, unit PAUT-4, which is calibrated for 10 mm carbon steel. Focus the scan on a fifteen-centimeter band centered on the weld crown, with particular attention to the section between markings 7.2m and 7.8m from the forward nozzle. If you find any indication with an amplitude exceeding 40% DAC, pause and capture the full A-scan data set before proceeding. Do not, however, remove the existing insulation layer on the vessel exterior; the inspection must be performed through the designated access ports in the insulation jacket only.

If no reportable indications are found, you may proceed with a re-test after obtaining a sign-off from Inspector Malik. The re-test pressure must be reduced to 20.3 MPa, and the hold time extended to ninety minutes. Conversely, if you find one or more indications above the reporting level, do not commence any repair. Isolate the vessel by closing master valve MV-11 and tag it with a red 'Hold for Engineering' label. Then, immediately transmit all collected data to the central diagnostics server under project ID 'C18A_Gamma_Assess'. The priority for this analysis is high, so please complete the inspection and report your findings by 16:00 today.

benchmarks.name: Farming data
benchmarks.original:
North Ridge Block 9A final nutrient audit is complete. The EnviroScan unit logged a median soil nitrate concentration of 18.2 ppm, but with high spatial variance. The two low-yield zones you flagged, designated LZ-7 and LZ-11, registered at 9.8 ppm and 8.1 ppm respectively, both below the 12 ppm intervention threshold. The main block's phosphorus is adequate at 28 kg/ha, but potassium is trending low at 135 kg/ha. The organic matter composite for the block is 3.1%.

Given these readings, please execute the variable-rate amendment protocol "VRA-9A-Supplement" for the next maintenance pass. The prescription map has been updated on the server with the tag "v4_final". Load only the polyammonium sulfate blend, product code AS-77, into the left-side spreader hopper. The target application rate for zones below 12 ppm nitrate is 42 kilograms per hectare. For all other areas of Block 9A, apply a maintenance rate of 15 kilograms per hectare. Under no circumstances should the blended potash mix (PK-30) be used for this pass; its application is deferred until the post-harvest window.

The operation must be completed before the forecasted rain event, which is now modeled to arrive at 18:00 local time on Thursday. Begin spreading no earlier than 10:00 Thursday to allow for morning dew evaporation. If the soil moisture sensor network shows any node above 35% volumetric water content at 09:00, delay commencement and await a manual override. Coordinate with the logistics agent for Silo 3; the required 1.8 metric tonnes of AS-77 have been allocated under batch identifier F23-8892. Confirm product scan against this batch ID prior to loading. The total allowable runtime for this application is capped at 4.5 hours to align with equipment scheduling. If the spreader's flow sensor deviates by more than 5% from the prescribed rate for over two minutes, pause the operation and generate an alert for field supervision.

benchmarks.name: Retail prose
benchmarks.original:
The refrigeration coil diagnostic on the main cold wall for the Delano’s Fresh Mart in Pinegrove just flagged a minor ammonia concentration spike at 0.8 ppm. Threshold for immediate shutdown is 2.0 ppm, so we’re in the advisory window. I need you to pull the activity logs from the last 72 hours for units FC-112A, FC-112B, and FC-118. The spike registered at 11:47 AM local. Cross-reference those logs with the scheduled defrost cycles—if any unit attempted a defrost between 10:00 AM and 1:00 PM today, hold off on its next scheduled defrost and switch it to manual-only mode for the next 48 hours. For any unit that didn’t attempt a defrost in that window, proceed with its next cycle as planned, but reduce the duration by 25%.

Now, regarding stock: the temperature in Bay 3 held steady at 34°F, so the integrity of the perishables there is confirmed. However, the high-value seafood shipment (PO #K7B-44902) for Chef Marlon’s special this weekend arrived early. It’s 40 lbs of live scallops and 15 lbs of black cod portions, currently in Bay 4 holding at 31°F. They must be moved to Bay 3 by 3:00 PM today, but only after you've completed the log pull and initial assessment on the coils. Do not commingle them with the existing halibut stock in the lower left section of Bay 3; use the upper right racks labeled “Reserved – M.” If the diagnostic shows a second spike above 1.2 ppm before the move, prioritize relocating the seafood to the backup cryo unit in Receiving first, then continue with the coil analysis. The store manager, Erica Vance, has been notified but is currently off-site until 4 PM. Your final summary to her needs to include the log findings, the action taken on each freezer coil unit, and the final location of the seafood shipment.

benchmarks.name: Software task
benchmarks.original:
The backup verification routine for the Vanta cluster is failing due to a signature mismatch in the manifest file. The primary error is in the 'core-indexer' component; its checksum, currently recorded as `9f3b7a1e8c2d`, should actually be `9f3b7a1e8c2f`. The last two digits are flipped. You need to push a corrected manifest to the backup coordinator at `coord-8.vanta.ops` before the next verification window, which is scheduled for 03:45 UTC. If the mismatch persists past 04:00 UTC, the system will escalate to a Tier-2 alert and automatically initiate a full re-sync of the past 24 hours, which will consume about 350 gigs of bandwidth from the Frankfurt node.

The manifest ID in question is `BKUP-2025-03-14-0342`. Please update only the checksum for 'core-indexer'; do not modify the timestamps or the entries for 'query-engine' and 'log-aggregator'. After pushing the manifest, trigger a manual pre-check using command sequence `VFY --id BKUP-2025-03-14-0342 --preflight`. This pre-check should take no longer than 120 seconds. If the pre-check passes, you will receive a confirmation digest. If it fails with a 'validation timeout' error, wait exactly 90 seconds and retry the pre-check once. Do not attempt a third time; instead, roll back to the previous manifest, version `1.4.2`, and notify me directly. The priority is to avoid the full re-sync, so if it's 03:50 UTC and the pre-check is still failing, bypass it and push the corrected manifest anyway, then monitor the 03:45 verification job's logs for a `SIG_SUCCESS` flag.

Also, please note that the Frankfurt node's bandwidth allocation for this job is capped at 500 gigabits for the entire maintenance cycle. If the pre-check succeeds but the live verification at 03:45 still fails for any reason, check the current bandwidth consumption for transaction ID `TX-88773`. If it shows over 475 gigabits used, pause any non-essential dataflows tagged with `env: staging` in that region until after the verification window closes.
